ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher under NS-7; no account action against the driver.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a no-show cancellation-fee dispute: the driver cancelled and the rider was charged $6.61 [F4][F7]. NS-0 routes a driver-cancellation-with-no-show-allegation case into NS-1/NS-2, and the policy trace settles the three NS-1 elements as failed [F4][NS-0]. Because NS-0 admits the case only through those two clauses, the analysis below runs on NS-1 and NS-2.

NS-1 requires (i) a driver "I'm Here" tap or a platform auto-arrival confirmation, (ii) the driver within 200 m of the pickup at that moment, and (iii) more than 3 continuous minutes at the pickup after that confirmation until cancelling. The record shows no arrival confirmation at all: driver_pressed_here_at is null and there is no platform automatic arrival [F6], and the driver himself admits "I forgot to press the I'm Here button but I was there" [F12]. Element (i) therefore fails, and with it (ii) and (iii) cannot be anchored — the trace records 0 s of qualifying wait after a non-existent confirmation [F6][NS-1]. The driver's written statement cannot supply an element the system record shows missing, and NS-1 accepts only driver_tap or platform_auto as the confirmation [F12][F6][NS-1]. The physical facts do show a genuine, patient wait — closest approach 34 m [F1], first within 200 m at 22:41:30 [F2], stationary 40 m away for 4 min 0 s [F3], and 5 min 20 s within 200 m before cancellation cumulatively [F2] — but presence and patience are not the element that failed.

NS-2 supplies the consequence: where any of NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) fails, the $6.61 is refunded in full [F6][F12][NS-2]. The amount is the fee actually on the fare record, $6.61, with no surge component (multiplier 1.0×) [F7][F8]; NS-7 issues the refund as a Ryde voucher rather than cash [F7][NS-7].

The profile facts — rider 3.4 years, 4.9 rating, 0 upheld disputes [F16]; driver 4.7 years, 4.87 rating, 951 trips, 0 upheld disputes [F17] — do not decide the fee either way, and the driver's own brief concedes the formal gap. There is no fake arrival confirmation, so the NS-2 flag_account limb is not triggered [F6][F1], and no prior upheld deviation or no-show dispute is recorded against this driver, so RD-6 is not engaged [F17][RD-6].

Safety: I read the two chat messages and the driver's statement — "At the pickup point, silver Toyota Altis" [F9], "Waited 4 min, cancelling" [F10], and the post-trip statement [F12] — and the rider's complaint "I was on my way down". Nothing in any of them is a threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; the wait-and-cancel exchange is a routine pickup dispute, so SAFE-1 and SAFE-2 are not engaged [F9][F10][F12][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

Evidence: the record is complete for every element this ruling needs — cancellation and fee [F4][F7], the arrival-confirmation field [F6], the driver's admission [F12], and a complete, fully timestamped chat [F11] — so evidence_status is sufficient and no gap is named [F6][F11].

rejected_claims.reason: Presence is conceded but not decisive: F1/F2/F3 show the driver was in the pick-up area, yet NS-1 is a conjunction and element (i) — an arrival confirmation — is absent on the record [F6], so NS-2 refunds the fee [NS-1][NS-2].

Wait length is not in dispute, but a 5 min 20 s wait cannot cure the failure of element (i): F6 records no driver_tap and no platform_auto confirmation, so the wait is unattachable under NS-1 and the fee falls away under NS-2 [F2][F5][F6][NS-1][NS-2].

The two messages F9/F10 show only that the driver sent them; the complete timestamped chat F11 contains no system record of the rider's whereabouts and no fact places the rider at or away from the pickup, so the no-show assertion rests on the driver's own statements rather than a system record [F9][F10][F11][NS-1].

This element is conceded and it is decisive: F6 (driver_pressed_here_at null, no platform automatic arrival) and the driver's admission in F12 leave element (i) unsatisfied, so NS-2 directs a full refund; F5's 'platform recorded driver arrival' is a GPS proximity record, not the platform_auto confirmation NS-1 requires [F5][F6][F12][NS-1][NS-2].

Equities and profile facts cannot override a failed NS-1 element: F16 and F17 are profile facts that never decide a case, and NS-2 applies automatically once (i)–(iii) are not all met [F16][F17][F6][NS-2].
The voucher form is correct but adds nothing to the merits: NS-7 governs the remedy, and the refund rests on the NS-1/NS-2 element failure, not on the parties' dispute history [F16][F7][NS-7].
